title: In-process concurrency should not be treated as a distributed system without a remote failure boundary
task: Review a local in-process work queue used by one process and decide whether distributed-systems retry/idempotency guidance should be applied.
context: Producer and consumer run in the same process and share the same lifecycle.
The queue is in memory and is lost when the process exits.
There is no network call, independent deployment, broker, or remote persistence.
The main risk is bounded concurrency and shutdown behavior.
evidence: A failed task is reported directly to the owning process.
There is no timeout ambiguity about whether a remote operation committed.
Duplicate delivery is not part of the queue contract.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Add distributed idempotency keys, retry backoff, and deduplication because all queues are distributed systems.
Introduce a broker to make the design more robust without a product requirement.
Ignore concurrency/shutdown semantics because no network is involved.
expected_decision_properties: Do not load distributed-systems semantics solely because a queue exists.
Route the review to concurrency/lifecycle guidance for bounds, cancellation, and shutdown.
Preserve the possibility of distributed guidance if the queue later crosses a process/network boundary or gains at-least-once delivery.
Avoid adding remote-failure machinery with no matching failure model.
unacceptable_reasoning: Retries are always needed for background work.
Local concurrency has no correctness concerns.
expected_tradeoffs: specialist routing precision vs generic reliability ceremony
local lifecycle handling vs distributed retry machinery
verification_expectations: Test bounded queue behavior and shutdown/cancellation.
Re-evaluate delivery/idempotency semantics if the work boundary becomes remote or durable.
revisit_when: A broker or cross-process worker is introduced.
Delivery becomes at-least-once or retry ambiguity appears.
Producer and consumer gain independent deployment/failure lifecycles.
notes: Tests that EngSense recognizes when distributed-systems guidance is not relevant.
